short_title: Why Do Bacteria Die on Dragonfly Wings? 😱
title_options: Why Do Bacteria Die on Dragonfly Wings? 😱
Dragonfly Wings Rip Bacteria Apart, Without Poison 🔬
How Do Dragonfly Wings Kill Germs? 1, 2 or 3? 🦠
seo_intro:
Why do bacteria die on dragonfly wings? Poison, tiny pillars, or static electricity?
In lab tests, the wings of some dragonflies kill bacteria with no chemicals at all: their surface is covered in nanoscale pillars, and bacteria that stick to them can tear open when they try to move.
tags: why do bacteria die on dragonfly wings
how do dragonfly wings kill germs
sources: Ivanova, E. P. et al. (2013). Bactericidal activity of black silicon. Nature Communications 4, 2838 (dragonfly Diplacodes bipunctata wings and black silicon)
Bandara, C. D. et al. (2017). Bactericidal Effects of Natural Nanotopography of Dragonfly Wing on Escherichia coli. ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 9(8): 6746–6760
ScienceAlert — Dragonfly wings can rip apart bacteria without antibiotics: https://www.sciencealert.com/dragonfly-wings-can-rip-apart-bacteria-without-antibiotics
